description: Use when narrowing access that sharing already granted. Trigger keywords: restriction rule, recordFilter, userCriteria, RestrictionRule metadata, hide records, restrict visibility. NOT for list-view scope only - use admin/scoping-rules.
inputs: Target object API name, confirmed against the supported targetEntity list for enforcementType Restrict
Which users the rule applies to, expressed as one EQUALS test on a $User field (ProfileId, UserRoleId, IsActive, UserType)
Which records those users keep, expressed as one EQUALS test on a record field
Org edition — the active-rule ceiling differs between Enterprise/Developer and Performance/Unlimited
An inventory of who holds View All / View All Data / Modify All / Modify All Data on the object, and which Apex or integration paths run in system mode
name: restriction-rules
official_sources: Restriction Rules Developer Guide — Considerations (supported objects; 2 active per object in Enterprise and Developer, 5 in Performance and Unlimited; "Restriction rules aren't applied for code executed in System Mode"; View All / Modify All bypass; "The UserRecordAccess object doesn't consider whether a user's access is blocked due to a restriction rule"; calendar Show Details; subordinates' events; global search shortcuts; Chatter publisher; EQUALS-only operator; no AND/OR/formulas; 15-character Ids; supported data types; custom picklist values supported in record and user criteria, and deleting one means "the rule no longer works as intended"; only one "dot" (one lookup level from the targetEntity); null/blank values unsupported; lookup to a missing related record denies access; parent rule does not restrict children; "create only one restriction or scoping rule per object per user"; change set or unlocked package deployment and cross-org Id remapping; external object adapter support and additional database calls; three-to-five percent record-filter overhead on large data volumes; Salesforce Classic prerequisite) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.restriction_rules.meta/restriction_rules/restriction_rules_considerations.htm (verified 2026-08-15)

Restriction Rules Developer Guide — Restriction Rules ("When a restriction rule is applied to a user, the records that the user is granted access to via org-wide defaults, sharing rules, and other sharing mechanisms are filtered by criteria that you specify"; "the data that they had read access to via your sharing settings is further scoped to only records matching the recordFilter"; "If you create two active rules, and both rules apply to a given user, only one of the active rules is observed") — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.restriction_rules.meta/restriction_rules/restriction_rules_about.htm (verified 2026-08-15)

Restriction Rules Developer Guide — About This Guide ("Restriction rules are a record-level access control mechanism that allows you to grant granular visibility to specified users"; Lightning Experience in Enterprise, Performance, Unlimited, and Developer editions) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.restriction_rules.meta/restriction_rules/restriction_rules_intro.htm (verified 2026-08-15)

Restriction Rules Developer Guide — RestrictionRule (Metadata API) (suffix `.rule`, directory `restrictionRules`, API version 52.0 and later; required fields `description`, `enforcementType`, `masterLabel`, `recordFilter`, `targetEntity`, `userCriteria`, `version`; `active` defaults to false; enum values "FieldRestrict—Don't use.", "Restrict—Restriction rule.", "Scoping—Scoping rule."; supported `targetEntity` per enforcement type; Manage Sharing and View Restriction and Scoping Rules permissions) — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.restriction_rules.meta/restriction_rules/meta_restrictionrule.htm (verified 2026-08-15)

Salesforce Engineering — "Restriction Rules: Complementing Salesforce's Record Access Control Mechanism" (rules are not materialised into the sharing tables: "Rather than store access in the Sharing Tables, we thought, why not generate an Access Control Policy that could be read at runtime to define access?" and "we make just one call to the Decision Engine, which will then return a filter. Whilst querying for the data, we add that filter to the query, thereby eliminating records the user does not have access to.") — https://engineering.salesforce.com/restriction-rules-820f2218a51b/ (verified 2026-08-15)

Scoping Rules Developer Guide — Considerations ("Create up to two active scoping rules per object in Developer editions. Create up to five active scoping rules per object in Performance and Unlimited editions" — no Enterprise number is stated, and this ceiling is counted separately from the restriction-rule ceiling; list views and reports; "Create only one scoping or restriction rule per object per user") — https://developer.salesforce.com/docs/atlas.en-us.scoping_rules.meta/scoping_rules/scoping_rules_considerations.htm (verified 2026-08-15)

The exact Setup click path to the Restriction Rules node. The Developer Guide says only "set up restriction rules in Salesforce by navigating to a supported object in the Object Manager," and the fuller Setup instructions live on a Salesforce Help page that does not fetch. This skill therefore describes the metadata and API paths, which are fully sourced, and does not invent a click trail.

Behaviour of `enforcementType` `FieldRestrict`. The Metadata API reference lists it as an enum value and says exactly one thing about it — "FieldRestrict—Don't use." — which this skill repeats verbatim and the checker enforces. No page reached during authoring describes what the value actually does, so nothing further is claimed about it.
The release in which restriction rules reached GA. API version 52.0 is sourced as the first version supporting the metadata type; the marketing GA release is not, so it is not stated.
outputs: Deployable RestrictionRule metadata (.rule) with enforcementType, targetEntity, userCriteria, recordFilter and version
A written bypass inventory naming every documented path around the rule and who currently holds it
A test plan that proves the filter in the record UI, in a report, and in SOQL as the restricted user
A deployment plan covering change set or unlocked package delivery and cross-org Id remapping
